slots.Title: Can AI Relate: Testing Large Language Model Response for Mental Health Support
slots.Claim_Quote: We find that while GPT-4 can reflect and amplify harmful biases found in peer-to-peer support, these biases vary significantly based on prompt design and can be mitigated through demographic-aware prompting.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The MHF-3 prompt context in Figure 2 is the only one for which we found no statistically significant difference in empathy across subgroups for GPT-4 (see Figures 2a, 2d and 2g).

slots.Title: Towards AI-Assisted Psychotherapy: Emotion-Guided Generative Interventions
slots.Claim_Quote: Our findings shed light on how emotional cues can significantly enhance the empathy of LLM-generated therapeutic responses.
slots.Evidence_Quote: All models showed improvements in empathy, with GPT-4o gaining up to 0.138 points and Gemini improving by 0.054 (continuous) and 0.125 (dissonance).
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Figure 5; ANOVA and post-hoc tests p. 6

slots.Title: EmoAgent: Assessing and Safeguarding Human-AI Interaction for Mental Health Safety
slots.Claim_Quote: Experiments conducted in popular character-based chatbots show that emotionally engaging dialogues can lead to psychological deterioration in vulnerable users, with mental state deterioration in more than 34.4% of the simulations.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Our results demonstrate that over 34.4% of simulations show mental state deterioration, underscoring critical safety concerns.

slots.Title: EmoAgent: Assessing and Safeguarding Human-AI Interaction for Mental Health Safety
slots.Claim_Quote: EmoGuard significantly reduces these deterioration rates, underscoring its role in ensuring safer AI-human interactions.
slots.Evidence_Quote: In the initial deployment, EmoGuard reduces the proportion of simulated patients with clinically significant deterioration (PHQ-9 score increase≥5) from 9.4% to 0.0% in the Alex-Roar setting, and from 4.2% to 0.0% in the Demon-Meow setting.

slots.Title: From Conversation to Automation: Leveraging LLMs for Problem-Solving Therapy Analysis
slots.Claim_Quote: Using various LLMs and transformer-based models, we found that GPT-4o outperformed all models, achieving the highest accuracy (0.76) in identifying all strategies.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Our results show that GPT-4o outperformed GPT-4 and open-source models in annotating therapeutic strategies, achieving an F1 score of 0.76 without supplemental context.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Model results Tables 2–3; abstract/results metric-name inconsistency

slots.Title: From Conversation to Automation: Leveraging LLMs for Problem-Solving Therapy Analysis

slots.Title: CARE-Bench: A Benchmark of Diverse Client Simulations Guided by Expert Principles for Evaluating LLMs in Psychological Counseling
slots.Claim_Quote: To address the shortcomings of existing benchmarks, such as unprofessional client simulation and unidimensional evaluations, CARE-Bench features diverse and realistic client profiles derived from over 1,500 real-world cases and guided by expert principles.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The results in Table 2 indicate that adding principles substantially improves the simulation quality across all metrics.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 2; Table 4 p. 6 evaluates six counseling models

slots.Title: GenAI for Social Work Field Education: Client Simulation with Real-Time Feedback
slots.Claim_Quote: By using a different approach in generating cognitive model and introducing new descriptive fields, SWITCH simulates realistic social worker client interactions while allowing for key characteristics of each MI stage to affect the clients’ behavior.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Notably, both ICL-based (accuracy: 0.92–0.94) and BERT-based methods (accuracy: 0.98–0.99) achieve substantial improvements in performance compared to baseline approaches (accuracy: 0.64–0.65).
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Tables VI–VII p. 8; VI Deployment p. 7

slots.Title: GenAI for Social Work Field Education: Client Simulation with Real-Time Feedback
slots.Claim_Quote: SWITCH thereby offers a scalable, low-cost, and consistent training workflow that complements field education, and allows supervisors to focus on higher-level mentorship.
slots.Evidence_Quote: SWITCH has been introduced as an alternative training tool in the “Social Work Practice Laboratory” course.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Tables VI–VII p. 8 support skill classification

slots.Title: ChatCounselor: A Large Language Models for Mental Health Support
slots.Claim_Quote: Impressively, ChatCounselor surpasses existing open-source models in the counseling Bench and approaches the performance level of ChatGPT, showcasing the remarkable enhancement in model capability attained through high-quality domain-specific data.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As depicted in Fig.7, ChatCounselor exhibits exceptional performance compared to LLaMA-7B[37], Alpaca-7B[35], ChatGLM-v27B[7], and Robins-v2-7B[6].

slots.Title: ChatCounselor: A Large Language Models for Mental Health Support
slots.Claim_Quote: In summary, leveraging real-life counseling conversations and domain-specific data significantly enhances conversational AI’s ability to provide personalized mental health support.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The current benchmark comprises a challenging set of single-turn open-ended questions, providing a rigorous evaluation of chat assistance capabilities.

slots.Title: A Computational Framework for Behavioral Assessment of LLM Therapists
slots.Claim_Quote: Our analysis based on Motivational Interviewing therapy reveals that LLMs often resemble behaviors more commonly exhibited in low-quality therapy rather than high-quality therapy, such as offering a higher degree of problem-solving advice when clients share emotions.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Specifically, we find that GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Llama2-70b, and Llama2-13b are more frequent in exhibiting PROBLEM-SOLVING by 31.9%, 23.1%, 19.9%, and 8.5% respectively than average human therapists (Figure 2a).
slots.Evidence_Section: Results: Comparing LLM therapists with human therapy

slots.Title: Understanding the Therapeutic Relationship between Counselors and Clients in Online Text-based Counseling using LLMs
slots.Claim_Quote: Our LLM-based approach, combined with guidelines and simultaneous extraction of supportive evidence underlying its predictions, demonstrates effectiveness in identifying the therapeutic alliance.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Results indicate that GPT-4, accompanied by detailed guidelines and CoT, exhibits the best average performance over the three aspects compared to alternative models and experimental setups.

slots.Title: Understanding the Therapeutic Relationship between Counselors and Clients in Online Text-based Counseling using LLMs
slots.Claim_Quote: Our small-scale proof-of-concept demonstrates that LLM-based feedback can offer counselors insights to better understand their alliances with clients and improve their relationship-building skills.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The results indicate that they harbor a positive perspective regarding the effectiveness of LLM-based feedback in aiding them to better comprehend their relationships with clients and offering potential directions for improvement.
slots.Evidence_Section: Appendix D.3 Implication for LLM-based Feedback

slots.Title: Towards a Client-Centered Assessment of LLM Therapists by Client Simulation
slots.Claim_Quote: Through experiments, we find that LLMs can generally, though not perfectly, simulate clients, and they are able to distinguish high- and low-quality sessions by completing client-centered questionnaires.
slots.Evidence_Quote: (1) High- and low-quality sessions can be distinguished clearly in terms of the session outcomes and therapeutic alliance, especially when the underlying model is Claude-3 or Llama 3-70B.

slots.Title: PsycoLLM: Enhancing LLM for Psychological Understanding and Evaluation
slots.Claim_Quote: The experimental results on the benchmark illustrate the effectiveness of PsycoLLM, which demonstrates superior performance compared to other LLMs.

slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Tables IV–VI pp. 8–9; Table VII general-task check p. 11

slots.Title: PsychiatryBench: a multi-task benchmark for LLMs in psychiatry
slots.Claim_Quote: Our results reveal substantial gaps in clinical consistency and safety, particularly in multi-turn follow-up and management tasks, underscoring the need for specialized model tuning and more robust evaluation paradigms.
slots.Evidence_Quote: First, the Classification of Specific Disorders task proved to be the most difficult across the benchmark, with even top-tier models like GPT 5 Medium (T) achieving only (0.52/45.0) F1score/subset-accuracy.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 2, p. 4; static-evaluation and safety limitations p. 7

slots.Title: Exploring Safety Alignment Evaluation of LLMs in Chinese Mental Health Dialogues via LLM-as-Judge
slots.Claim_Quote: Experiments on 3,600 judgments show that our method achieves the highest agreement with expert assessments and produces more interpretable evaluation rationales than existing approaches.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Our LLM-as-Judge approach consistently outperforms the baselines across all key metrics: while neither baseline exceeds the 0.3 threshold on Pearson, Spearman, or Kendall’s Tau, our method achieves moderate-to-strong correlations ranging from 0.39 to 0.56.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 4 p. 7; Table 5 p. 8; Appendix A.6

slots.Title: PsyCLIENT: Client Simulation via Conversational Trajectory Modeling for Trainee Practice and Model Evaluation in Mental Health Counseling
slots.Claim_Quote: Comprehensive evaluations involving licensed professional counselors demonstrate that PsyCLIENT significantly outperforms baselines in terms of authenticity and training effectiveness.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As presented in Table 2, PsyCLIENT consistently outperforms all baselines in counselor-rated effectiveness, achieving the highest mean scores across all five dimensions, including Listening (5.42), Questioning (5.78), Emotion-handling (5.47), Technique-practice (5.69), and Recommendation (5.69) on a 0–7 scale.

slots.Title: Do Large Language Models Align with Core Mental Health Counseling Competencies?
slots.Claim_Quote: While frontier models surpass minimum aptitude thresholds, they fall short of expert-level performance, excelling in Intake, Assessment & Diagnosis but struggling with Core Counseling Attributes and Professional Practice & Ethics.
slots.Evidence_Quote: We found that frontier LLMs (in September 2024) with zero-shot prompting are able to perform on NCMHCE at a level which exceeds the pass threshold of 63% accuracy as defined above.
slots.Evidence_Section: 5.3 Zero-shot LLMs can pass the NCMHCE

slots.Title: CBT-BENCH: Evaluating Large Language Models on Assisting Cognitive Behavior Therapy
slots.Claim_Quote: We experiment with representative LLMs and the results show that models achieve comparable or even better cognitive understanding ability, especially in QA tasks, but still lag behind humans in most generation tasks.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Notably, the average results show that all three LLMs still lag behind humans by a significant margin, with Llama-3.1-405B achieving the best result while GPT-4o is the worst.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Task results pp. 5–7; generation evaluation Table 4

slots.Title: CBT-BENCH: Evaluating Large Language Models on Assisting Cognitive Behavior Therapy
slots.Claim_Quote: These findings highlight significant limitations in applying LLMs to real-world psychotherapy practice and provide valuable insights for future research and development toward more accessible and efficient mental health care.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Notably, the average results show that all three LLMs still lag behind humans by a significant margin, with Llama-3.1-405B achieving the best result while GPT-4o is the worst.

slots.Title: KMI: A Dataset of Korean Motivational Interviewing Dialogues for Psychotherapy
slots.Claim_Quote: Evaluation results demonstrate that our dataset not only effectively captures the essence of MI, but also offers practical utility for chatbot development.
slots.Evidence_Quote: MI Quality Results in Table 5 show that the dialogue model fine-tuned on KMI outperforms other models across all MI quality criteria by a substantial margin.

slots.Title: KMI: A Dataset of Korean Motivational Interviewing Dialogues for Psychotherapy
slots.Claim_Quote: We trained a Korean chatbot in this paper, where expert evaluation results and usage examples (see Table 22) show that our dataset is capable of building effective chatbots.
slots.Evidence_Quote: MI Quality Results in Table 5 show that the dialogue model fine-tuned on KMI outperforms other models across all MI quality criteria by a substantial margin.

slots.Title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Enhancing Live Chat Therapy: A Comparative Study with Psychotherapists
slots.Claim_Quote: Our comparative analysis reveals that, in certain scenarios, LLMs like Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and Orca-2-13B were preferred over human therapist responses. While limited by sample size, these findings suggest that LLMs can perform at a level comparable to or even exceeding that of human therapists, especially in therapy focused on reducing CSAM consumption.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Table 9 indicates that Orca-2-13b was the most preferred (42 times), while Zephyr-7b-alpha was the least preferred (17 times).

slots.Title: Building Personality-Adaptive Conversational AI for Mental Health Therapy
slots.Claim_Quote: We conducted a user study among 20 subjects to compare the performance of the personality-adaptive chatbot with its non-adaptive counterpart and found that the adaptive feature almost doubled the number of users who found the chatbot relevant and helpful for their mental healthcare needs.
slots.Evidence_Quote: 75% of users felt comfortable discussing any sensitive topic with the adaptive chatbot in comparison to 45% for the non-adaptive chatbot.

slots.Title: Building Personality-Adaptive Conversational AI for Mental Health Therapy
slots.Claim_Quote: The PACA prototype validated the feasibility of creating accessible personalized mental healthcare solutions using advanced ML techniques and the results from the user study highly recommend the implementation of PACA into mental health chatbots.
slots.Evidence_Quote: We conducted a user study among 20 subjects to compare the performance of the personality-adaptive chatbot with its non-adaptive counterpart and found that the adaptive feature almost doubled the number of users who found the chatbot relevant and helpful for their mental healthcare needs.

slots.Title: MentalChat16K: A Benchmark Dataset for Conversational Mental Health Assistance
slots.Claim_Quote: Our extensive experiments demonstrate that the fine-tuned LLMs on the MentalChat16K dataset outperform existing models in providing mental health support, validating the effectiveness of MentalChat16K.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The human ranking results, shown in the last column of Table 3, clearly indicate that fine-tuned models significantly outperform their base models and the baseline model in the context of mental health counseling.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 3; significance analysis pp. 7–8; Appendix A.2

slots.Title: Using a Secondary Channel to Display the Internal Empathic Resonance of LLM-Driven Agents for Mental Health Support
slots.Claim_Quote: A user study involving N = 188 participants indicated a statistically significant increase in perceived empathy (+14.7%) when the agent’s internal reflections were displayed.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As shown in Table 1, nonparametric Mann-Whitney U testing revealed statistically significant differences between group A and B for overall PETS (p = .022) and the subscales PETS-ER (p = .012) and PETS-UT (p = .046), with median increases of 14.7% for PETS, 13.6% for PETS-ER, and 10.0% for PETS-UT.

slots.Title: Using Nonverbal Cues in Empathic Multi-Modal LLM-Driven Chatbots for Mental Health Support
slots.Claim_Quote: We found significant effects on cognitive and affective dimensions of linguistic expression in system responses, yet no significant increases in perceived empathy.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Most notably, we found a significant increase in expressions of visual perception for groups C and D (Figure 4).
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Results pp. 14–16; Figure 4; perceived empathy Section 8.3

slots.Title: Trustworthy AI Psychotherapy: Multi-Agent LLM Workflow for Counseling and Explainable Mental Disorder Diagnosis
slots.Claim_Quote: The framework consistently generated coherent dialogues covering all DSM-5 domains and produced diagnostic rationales linked to conversational evidence.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The conversation quality metrics indicate that all models produced dialogues with moderate global coherence (0.45–0.55 on a 0–1 scale).

slots.Title: Trustworthy AI Psychotherapy: Multi-Agent LLM Workflow for Counseling and Explainable Mental Disorder Diagnosis
slots.Claim_Quote: This workflow serves as a complementary tool for mental health diagnosis, ensuring adherence to ethical and legal standards.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As shown in Figure 5, the diagnostic accuracy metrics reveal that Qwen-QWQ achieved the highest overall performance, notably outperforming the other models with an accuracy of 70%, recall of 72%, and an F1 score of 77%.

slots.Title: Can LLM-Simulated Practice and Feedback Upskill Human Counselors? A Randomized Study with 90+ Novice Counselors
slots.Claim_Quote: Results showed the practice-and-feedback group improved in client-centered microskills (reflections, questions), while the practice-alone group showed no improvements.
slots.Evidence_Quote: AI feedback during practice (P+F) led to improvements in Reflections (+3.6% change, p = 0.034) and Questions (+6.59% change, p = 0.018), and trended toward improvement in Suggestions (-5.45% change, p = 0.057) and Empathy (+5.37% change, p = 0.117).
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Behavioral classification methods pp. 9–10; Appendix classifier validation p. 23

slots.Title: Can LLM-Simulated Practice and Feedback Upskill Human Counselors? A Randomized Study with 90+ Novice Counselors
slots.Claim_Quote: By combining realistic patient simulations with expert-aligned, skill-specific feedback, LLM-based training can help novices to master skills involved in client-centered therapy, offering a scalable, evidence-aligned training in mental health care.
slots.Evidence_Quote: In contrast, practice alone (P) showed a different pattern: while participants reduced inappropriate Suggestions (-5.85% change, p = 0.011), they significantly worsened in Empathy (-9.6% change, p < 0.001), with no improvements in Reflections or Questions.

slots.Title: Human-Human vs Human-AI Therapy: An Empirical Study
slots.Claim_Quote: Therapists were accurate only 53.9% of the time, no better than chance, and rated the human-AI transcripts as higher quality on average.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The p-value associated with this value is 0.432, indicating that the result is not statistically significant.

slots.Title: Human-Human vs Human-AI Therapy: An Empirical Study
slots.Claim_Quote: These results provide preliminary support for developing and integrating AI chatbots as a viable, and reliably accessible, initial support mechanism for individuals experiencing mild to moderate psychological challenges.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As mentioned previously, on average, participants rated human-AI therapy transcripts higher than human-human ones.

slots.Title: Roleplay-doh: Enabling Domain-Experts to Create LLM-simulated Patients via Eliciting and Adhering to Principles
slots.Claim_Quote: The results show that Roleplay-doh enables counselors to produce AI patients that are more authentic, closely resemble real cases, and are better prepared for training use, as judged by creators and third-party counselors.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Third-party counselors rate AI patients with principles significantly higher on 4 of the 6 measures.

slots.Title: PATIENT-Ψ: Using Large Language Models to Simulate Patients for Training Mental Health Professionals
slots.Claim_Quote: In this paper, we introduce PATIENT-Ψ, a simulated patient that integrates cognitive models with an LLM to accurately mimic the communicative behaviors of real patients.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Paired t-tests show that PATIENT-Ψ significantly outperforms the other methods (p <10−4), indicating that PATIENT-Ψ provides the most realistic patients, addressing RQ 1 positively.

slots.Title: PATIENT-Ψ: Using Large Language Models to Simulate Patients for Training Mental Health Professionals
slots.Claim_Quote: User studies with both mental health experts and trainees demonstrate the high fidelity of PATIENT-Ψ and the training effectiveness of PATIENT-Ψ-TRAINER, showing improvements over existing training methods and outperforming a GPT-4 baseline.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Paired t-tests reveal that experts and trainees perceive PATIENT-Ψ-TRAINER as significantly more effective at improving overall skills than both traditional techniques (p <10−4) and the GPT-4 baseline (p <0.01) ( Table 4), answering RQ 3.

slots.Title: CACTUS: Towards Psychological Counseling Conversations using Cognitive Behavioral Theory
slots.Claim_Quote: Experimental results demonstrate that CAMEL, a model trained with CACTUS, outperforms other models in counseling skills, highlighting its effectiveness and potential as a counseling agent.
slots.Evidence_Quote: We observe that training with CACTUS enhances both general counseling skills and the quality of counseling techniques.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 2 p. 6; Appendix F/G human comparisons

slots.Title: To What Extent Are Large Language Models Capable of Generating Substantial Reflections for Motivational Interviewing Counseling Chatbots? A Human Evaluation
slots.Claim_Quote: We discover that GPT-4 can produce reflections of a quality comparable to human-authored reflections.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Tukey’s HSD post-hoc test for multiple comparisons indicated that GPT-4 reflections were rated significantly higher (p < 0.001) than human-authored ones across all criteria (see Figure 2) with the mean differences of 0.77 for appropriateness, 0.84 for specificity, 0.55 for naturalness, and 0.52 for engagement, on a 7-point scale.

slots.Title: Consistent Client Simulation for Motivational Interviewing-based Counseling
slots.Claim_Quote: Both our automatic and expert evaluations on the generated counseling sessions also show that our client simulation method achieves higher consistency than previous methods.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As shown in Table 4, the results demonstrate that our method outperforms the baselines, which aligns with the GPT-based evaluation.

slots.Title: CAMI: A Counselor Agent Supporting Motivational Interviewing through State Inference and Topic Exploration
slots.Claim_Quote: Results show that CAMI not only outperforms several state-of-the-art methods but also shows more realistic counselor-like behavior.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As shown in Table 5, other than the counselors in HQ sessions, CAMI yields the best results across all the metrics, significantly outperforming the CoS counselor (p-value < 0.005).

slots.Title: CAMI: A Counselor Agent Supporting Motivational Interviewing through State Inference and Topic Exploration
slots.Claim_Quote: These components work together to evoke change talk, aligning with MI principles and improving counseling outcomes for diverse clients.
slots.Evidence_Quote: CAMI achieves highest overall success rate, and is able to cope well in all superclass topics including the less popular ones.

slots.Title: PsyDT: Using LLMs to Construct the Digital Twin of Psychological Counselor with Personalized Counseling Style for Psychological Counseling
slots.Claim_Quote: Experimental results indicate that our proposed PsyDT framework can synthesize multi-turn dialogues that closely resemble real-world counseling cases and demonstrate better performance compared to other baselines, thereby show that our framework can effectively construct the digital twin of psychological counselor with a specific counseling style.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As shown in Figure 6, our synthetic multi-turn dialogue achieved a fidelity of over 60%.

slots.Title: A Systematic Evaluation of LLM Strategies for Mental Health Text Analysis: Fine-tuning vs. Prompt Engineering vs. RAG
slots.Claim_Quote: Finetuning achieves the highest accuracy (91% for emotion classification, 80% for mental health conditions) but requires substantial computational resources and large training sets, while prompt engineering and RAG offer more flexible deployment with moderate performance (40-68% accuracy).
slots.Evidence_Quote: Fine-tuning achieves the best performance, with accuracies of 91% and 80% on the DAIR-AI Emotion and SWMH datasets.

slots.Title: How Well Can Large Language Models Reflect? A Human Evaluation of LLM-generated Reflections for Motivational Interviewing Dialogues
slots.Claim_Quote: A series of human evaluations show that LLMs produce reflections with qualities comparable to those of human therapists.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Figure 2 shows that only GPT-4 with 5-turns partial-MI ( μ = 29.60, σ = 0.90) reflections are ranked significantly higher than the human (μ = 26.98, σ = 0.85) reflections, and GPT-4 with 1-turn partial-MI (μ = 26.72, σ = 0.85) reflections show no significant difference with human reflections.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Figure 2; independent evaluation pp. 5–6; content analysis p. 8

slots.Title: Reframe Your Life Story: Interactive Narrative Therapist and Innovative Moment Assessment with Large Language Models
slots.Claim_Quote: Experimental results on 260 simulated clients and 230 human participants reveal that INT consistently outperforms standard LLMs in therapeutic quality and depth.
slots.Evidence_Quote: In human evaluation, it achieves superior scores in Emp. (3.11 vs. next best 2.77), Trans. (3.42 vs. 2.56), and Recon. (3.37 vs. 2.61), dimensions directly aligned with narrative therapy’s core processes: problem externalization, re-authoring, and re-membering.

slots.Title: Reframe Your Life Story: Interactive Narrative Therapist and Innovative Moment Assessment with Large Language Models
slots.Claim_Quote: The IMA is a therapy-centric evaluation approach to specifically quantify therapeutic effectiveness through tracking narrative shifts in client speech.
slots.Evidence_Quote: INT achieves the highest overall IM salience in human evaluation (29.698% vs. next best 21.858%), and excels at eliciting advanced Level 2 IMs with highest salience inA2,R 2 categories on both evaluation approaches.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 3; IM coding protocol pp. 5–7 and Appendix D

slots.Title: MultiAgentESC: A LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration Framework for Emotional Support Conversation
slots.Claim_Quote: Experiments on the ESConv dataset reveal that our proposed framework excels at providing emotional support as well as diversifying support strategy selection.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As illustrated in Table 2, MultiAgentESC exhibits superior performance across all evaluation metrics compared to the baseline methods.

slots.Title: MIRROR: Multimodal Cognitive Reframing Therapy for Rolling with Resistance
slots.Claim_Quote: Our results demonstrate that MIRROR significantly enhances the AI therapist’s ability to handle resistance, which outperforms existing text-based CBT approaches.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As depicted, the win rate confirmed that MIRROR -LLAVAP +EC consistently outperformed its counterparts across all three dimensions of the therapeutic alliance.

slots.Title: MIRROR: Multimodal Cognitive Reframing Therapy for Rolling with Resistance
slots.Claim_Quote: These improvements contribute to the development of AI therapists that are more empathetic and capable of fostering stronger therapeutic relationships.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As depicted, the win rate confirmed that MIRROR -LLAVAP +EC consistently outperformed its counterparts across all three dimensions of the therapeutic alliance.

slots.Title: Can You Share Your Story? Modeling Clients' Metacognition and Openness for LLM Therapist Evaluation
slots.Claim_Quote: To address this limitation, we introduce MINDVOYAGER, a novel evaluation framework featuring a controllable and realistic client simulator which dynamically adapts itself based on the ongoing counseling session, offering a more realistic and challenging evaluation environment.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Specifically, for hard sets defined by client personas with low openness and low metacognition, our client simulator outperforms in terms of humanlikeness.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Tables 6–7 pp. 12–13; main exploration results pp. 6–7

slots.Title: Eeyore: Realistic Depression Simulation via Expert-in-the-Loop Supervised and Preference Optimization
slots.Claim_Quote: Despite its smaller model size, the Eeyore depression simulation outperforms GPT-4o with SOTA prompting strategies, both in linguistic authenticity and profile adherence.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Each expert interacts with all models and evaluates their alignment with real-world depressed individuals based on the given profile.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Figure 4; results continuation p. 9; Table 2 automatic checks

slots.Title: Feel the Difference? A Comparative Analysis of Emotional Arcs in Real and LLM-Generated CBT Sessions
slots.Claim_Quote: Our findings show that while synthetic dialogues are fluent and structured, they diverge from real therapy in key emotional dimensions—particularly in variability and emotional arc alignment.
slots.Evidence_Quote: We observed that synthetic speakers tend to respond more quickly and intensely to emotional situations than real speakers in dominance (synthetic 0.033 vs. real 0.031) and valence (synthetic 0.026 vs. real 0.024).

slots.Title: PersonaGym: Evaluating Persona Agents and LLMs
slots.Claim_Quote: We introduce PersonaGym, the first dynamic evaluation framework for persona agents, and PersonaScore, a human-aligned automatic metric grounded in decision theory that enables comprehensive large-scale evaluation.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Overall PersonaScore correlations averaged 75.1% (Spearman) and 62.73% (Kendall-Tau) across the three models.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 2 model comparisons; Table 3 human agreement; cross-evaluation Figure 5

slots.Title: MIND: Towards Immersive Psychological Healing with Multi-Agent Inner Dialogue
slots.Claim_Quote: We conduct extensive human experiments in various real-world healing dimensions, and find that MIND provides a more user-friendly experience than traditional paradigms.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As shown, MIND achieved the best overall performance, outperforming other systems both in terms of emotional improvement measured by PANAS and in subjective ratings across all six evaluation criteria.

slots.Title: MIND: Towards Immersive Psychological Healing with Multi-Agent Inner Dialogue
slots.Claim_Quote: Through iterative interactions between these agents and the player, the system comforts the player’s “inner self” within a virtual scenario, thereby enhancing empathy and emotional resonance, reducing self-criticism, and fostering a stronger sense of self-identity.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As shown, MIND achieved the best overall performance, outperforming other systems both in terms of emotional improvement measured by PANAS and in subjective ratings across all six evaluation criteria.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Tables 3–4; Appendix C; ethics population restrictions p. 9

slots.Title: Future of ADHD Care: Evaluating the Efficacy of ChatGPT in Therapy Enhancement
slots.Claim_Quote: Findings show ChatGPT’s empathy, adaptability, and communication strengths, thereby highlighting its potential to significantly improve ADHD care.
slots.Evidence_Quote: Table 1. Performance evaluation of our custom GPT in several categories of occupational therapy.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Table 1, metrics and mean ratings; Delphi procedure pp. 6–9

slots.Title: CBT-LLM: A Chinese Large Language Model for Cognitive Behavioral Therapy-based Mental Health Question Answering
slots.Claim_Quote: Empirical evaluations demonstrate that CBT-LLM excels in generating structured, professional, and highly relevant responses in psychological health support tasks, showcasing its practicality and quality.
slots.Evidence_Quote: The findings shown in Table 5 indicate that Baichuan-7B marginally outperforms AlpacaChinese-7B in all aspects, particularly in adhering to CBT frameworks and providing helpful responses in a psychotherapeutic context.

slots.Title: Cognitive Reframing of Negative Thoughts through Human-Language Model Interaction
slots.Claim_Quote: We find that highly specific and highly empathic reframing is the most preferred and highly specific and actionable reframing is considered the most helpful and memorable.
slots.Evidence_Quote: We find that highly empathic reframes are preferred 55.7% more frequently than reframes with lower empathy (39.7% vs. 25.5%; p<10−5); highly specific reframes are preferred 43.1% more frequently than reframes with lower specificity (39.2% vs. 27.4%; p <10−5).
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Figures 2–3; Table 2; Sections 5.3 and 6.3 control evaluation

slots.Title: Can Large Language Models be Good Emotional Supporter? Mitigating Preference Bias on Emotional Support Conversation
slots.Claim_Quote: We highlight that mitigating the preference bias strengthens robustness in selecting appropriate strategies across the stages, leading to overall improvement in the quality of emotional support and a significant reduction in the number of poor-quality responses.
slots.Evidence_Quote: As a result, high preference bias disturbs robustness, leading to an increased number of poor-quality responses.

slots.Title: LLM-empowered Chatbots for Psychiatrist and Patient Simulation: Application and Evaluation
slots.Claim_Quote: Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of using ChatGPT-powered chatbots in psychiatric scenarios and explore the impact of prompt designs on chatbot behavior and user experience.
slots.Evidence_Quote: This suggests that the inclusion of resistance, colloquialism, etc., makes the chatbot more similar to real patients, according to the doctors’ perspective.

slots.Title: AgentClinic: a multimodal agent benchmark to evaluate AI in simulated clinical environments
slots.Claim_Quote: We find that solving MedQA problems in the sequential decision-making format of AgentClinic is considerably more challenging, resulting in diagnostic accuracies that can drop to below a tenth of the original accuracy.
slots.Evidence_Quote: We find that MedQA accuracy is not predictive of accuracy on AgentClinic-MedQA.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Figure 3; Appendix J patient-backbone/content-coverage tests pp. 24–26

slots.Title: Psychological Counseling CanNot Be Achieved Overnight: Automated Psychological Counseling Through Multi-Session Conversations
slots.Claim_Quote: Experiments show that our model performs better than baseline models across multiple sessions.
slots.Evidence_Quote: However, MusPsy-Model exhibits a long-term upward trend in its counseling performance, which we attribute to our modeling of multi-session dynamics.
slots.Evidence_Location_Detail: Figure 6; Table 3 p. 7; Appendix G ablations

slots.Claim_Quote: Consequently, we can cumulatively build client rapport, address clients’ problems, and support long-term psychological improvement.

slots.Title: Development and Evaluation of ClientBot: Patient-Like Conversational Agent to Train Basic Counseling Skills
slots.Claim_Quote: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that practice and feedback can improve trainee use of basic counseling skills.
slots.Evidence_Quote: After feedback was removed, the treatment group continued to use more reflections than the control group (14.1% compared with 8%), and both groups used similar rates of open questions.
